description: A tape delay with a fixed length of tape and a variable playback speed, so changing the speed changes the delay time and bends the pitch of whatever is already recorded on the tape

params.text: Sets the tape speed, from 0.1 to 2 times real time; the delay time is the tape length divided by this, so 0.5 gives twice the tape length and 2 gives half of it
Scales the delayed signal where it is added to the input, from none to 100%; that sum both goes back onto the tape and leaves the Out jack, so at zero Out carries the dry signal alone
Attenuates the voltage at the Speed input before it is added to the tape speed, passing none of it at the counter-clockwise end and all of it at the clockwise end

inputs.text: The signal recorded onto the tape, added to the delayed signal before it is written
Adds to the tape speed after the Amount knob attenuates it, 10V adding 1 to the speed; the sum is clamped between 0.1 and 2, and the scaling is linear in speed rather than in octaves
Replaces the signal read off the tape; patch an effect from Send to here to treat the delay inside the feedback loop

outputs.text: The input added to the delayed signal scaled by Feedback, which is the same mix that is written back onto the tape
The signal read off the tape, before the Return jack can replace it and before the feedback mix

notes: the tape is 100ms long until you pick another length from the module's menu, and nothing on the panel shows which length is in use
the signal written onto the tape passes a four-pole lowpass at the tape speed times half the sample rate, so it filters only below a speed of 1; the output has no filter and aliases above it
menu: Delay Buffer Size: 30 ms, 100 ms, 300 ms, 1 sec — sets the length of the tape, which is the delay time at a tape speed of 1

inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.2:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the signal read off the tape.
